items.title: Lifesaving breast cancer and endometriosis drug to be pulled from shelves
items.description: Patients have been left frustrated and scared after learning that a life-saving breast cancer and endometriosis drug is to be pulled from shelves in Australia and some other countries.

items.title: Breaking: Israel and Lebanon say they agree to ceasefire
items.description: Lebanon and Israel have agreed to a ceasefire, according to a joint statement with the United States.

items.title: Live: 'Ideological disagreement' between Australia and US on tariffs, PM says
items.description: Anthony Albanese says an "ideological disagreement" exists between Australia and the United States on tariffs, after Washington proposed slapping a 12.5 per cent tariff on Australian imports. Follow live.

items.title: Australia's economic slowdown is just beginning, experts warn
items.description: The economy grew just 0.3 per cent in the first quarter, gross domestic product per capita went backwards, and interest rate rises and cost-of-living pressures are weighing on households.

items.title: Why some home owners are at risk of slipping into negative equity
items.description: A 46-year-old former "forever renter" believes her house is now worth less than what she paid for it and she is at risk of slipping into negative equity, which would mean her Marrickville home could be worth less than what she owes the bank.

items.title: In a town where a baby died at a homeless campsite, charities say the data does not add up
items.description: As governments work to meet the growing need for social housing, community groups are stepping up to meet the rapidly increasing demand for their services to help fill the gap.

items.title: British PM urges calm after protests over handcuffed Henry Nowak's death
items.description: Video of officers ignoring the pleas of a dying, innocent man has sparked a political storm about how police treat ‌different ethnicities.

items.title: 'A little perturbed': Trump confirms expletive-laden call with Netanyahu
items.description: In an interview with a US podcast, the US president says he was frustrated that Benjamin Netanyahu was "constantly fighting with Lebanon".

items.title: Australia joins exclusive club granting access to advanced AI
items.description: Fresh access to AI deemed too dangerous for public release has ramped up pressure on the government to respond to possible risks.

items.title: Cannabis driving limit change to give 'freedom' to medicinal users in NSW
items.description: The Labor government plans to introduce a legal limit on the concentration of THC a driver can have in their system if they have a prescription.

items.title: Live: ASX to fall, SpaceX eyes mega IPO
items.description: The ASX is set to fall after Wall Street slipped overnight as hopes for a swift end to the war in Iran faded again. Follow the latest on our live markets blog.

items.title: Ban on travelling under bridge being reviewed amid refuelling debacle
items.description: Authorities are considering whether it is feasible for Australia's Antarctic icebreaker to safely travel under Hobart's Tasman Bridge, as the Tasmanian government tries to resolve a costly refuelling saga.

items.title: Sportsbet owner expands from gambling into less-regulated 'rewards club'
items.description: One of the world's biggest gambling companies is breaking into the 'rewards club' scene, raising the alarm among anti-gambling advocates.

items.title: World number one gutted after 'dirty' loss in French Open quarterfinal
items.description: Aryna Sabalenka feels the pain of a shock loss in the quarterfinals of the French Open, saying she just feels like smashing things.

items.title: Why healing from estrangement doesn't always mean reconciliation
items.description: Experts say healing might involve reducing emotional distress and gaining clarity from the situation.

items.title: 'My dreams came true': Oscar winner Sean Baker on finding success in his 50s
items.description: From his humble beginnings to winning a bevy of big awards, including four Oscars, the filmmaker has forged a successful career by staying true to his guiding principles.

items.title: Quiz: Can you recognise these 10 classic Australian album covers?
items.description: Take a closer look at some of the biggest albums in Australian music and tell us what you see.

items.title: A year since the varroa mite entered Qld, honey bee colonies have collapsed
items.description: Beekeepers in Queensland say they are 'barely hanging on' a year after the varroa mite was detected in the state for the first time.

items.title: Elderly NSW couple stabbed, alleged intruder shot during home invasion
items.description: A couple in their 70s have been critically injured and a man has been shot during a suspected home invasion in northern NSW this morning.

items.title: Ben went missing from his island home. His body has never been found
items.description: It's a tropical island, a few kilometres wide and known for being riddled with death adders. There's only one person who has ever gone missing from the island and never been found. An inquest is now trying to figure out what happened.

items.title: UN envoy intervenes in Woodside gas plant challenge
items.description: An independent expert has urged Australia to "make sure that things are done properly", while Woodside pushed back against her involvement.

items.title: 'Infuriating': Aboriginal voters turned away, told to line up again on SA election day
items.description: South Australia's Electoral Commission was aware that forcing First Nations voters to queue twice for the Voice election would be perceived as "discriminatory behaviour". Despite that, voters say it still happened and, in some cases, they were turned away.

items.title: Heatwaves are becoming so extreme, they're 'breaking the biology' of plants
items.description: Record-breaking heatwaves decimated crops in Australia this year and served as a "real wake up call" for the urgent need to develop more heat-resistant crops and research into food security. But it's not only in summer heatwaves are occurring and causing crops to fail.

items.title: Critical infrastructure in Western Sydney missing as funding plan comes to end
items.description: The M7-M12 interchange in Western Sydney is set to open soon, but advocates say the surrounding suburbs are still missing crucial infrastructure.

items.title: Tour operators brace for Kakadu site closures 'like COVID all over again'
items.description: Parks Australia has announced popular Kakadu attractions Jim Jim Falls and Twin Falls will remain closed for the rest of the year, with one tourism operator saying the closures will lead to a "very hard" tourism season.
